paras: The flogging of Jim Lawyer took place on the night of August 9, 1905, when about twenty men took Lawyer, a Black man, from a house near Bruceville, Texas, and whipped him. According to the only account, a Waco dispatch, he was punished for condemning the whites for the lynching of Sank Majors and was told to leave the area, which he did the next morning.

The flogging followed the lynching of Sank Majors, which the dispatch said was still the subject of "considerable feeling" in the county. Lawyer had made statements condemning the whites for that lynching.

On Wednesday night, about twenty men came for Lawyer near Bruceville, in the county of Waco. The San Antonio Daily Light placed him at "his neighbor's home," while the Bryan Morning Eagle's version of the same dispatch said he was taken from "his home" and called the men "white men." After hearing his statement, they gave him "a sound flogging" and told him "that it would be better for him to hunt other climes." Lawyer "took them at their word" and left on Thursday morning.
No report of arrests or of any official inquiry appears in the coverage. The dispatch closed instead with a warning that "further talk by the negroes will be to their own trouble."

The story reached print only in Texas, as a short item from Waco. The San Antonio Daily Light ran it first, on August 10, as a special under the headline "Negro Flogged for Denouncing Lynching." On August 11 the Bryan Morning Eagle printed it as "Whipped by Whites," with the subhead "Comments of Jim Lawyer, a Negro, Cause Him a Flogging," and the Palestine Daily Herald carried the same text among its state briefs.

None of these papers criticized the men who flogged Lawyer, and the Daily Light's version ended by warning other Black residents against further talk. No account of the flogging was found in the Black press.

accounts.label: Waco dispatch
accounts.gist: About twenty men called on Lawyer near Bruceville, heard his statement about the Majors lynching, flogged him and told him to leave; he left the next morning, and the dispatch warned that further talk by Black residents would bring trouble.

framing.detail: The San Antonio Daily Light headlined it 'Negro Flogged for Denouncing Lynching' and ended with a warning that 'further talk by the negroes will be to their own trouble', with no criticism of the floggers.
The Bryan Morning Eagle ran the same dispatch as 'Whipped by Whites. Comments of Jim Lawyer, a Negro, Cause Him a Flogging', and the Palestine Daily Herald reprinted it the same day.

conflicts.note: Both texts come from one Waco dispatch; the variance is likely an editing or transcription difference, and neither is better evidence.
